messages:
Tara L: FYI we rolled Sylph-v0.9-ptq into the canary lane. Perf Ok but structured toolcall parse rate jumped. ci-bot posted details: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/sylph-v0.9

Omar K: How big is the regression vs fp16?

Ivy (Canary): Summary from canary: samples=800, parse_fail=3.3% vs fp16 baseline 0.14%. Failure types: trailing-suffix (free-text), truncated-array, dangling-comma.

Sam: Snippet from a failing trace:
```
{"tool":"lookup","input":["deploy steps"]}
Also check the notes in the repo.
```
So JSON ends then model appends an extra sentence.

Tara L: Reproduced locally with streaming + kv-cache enabled, batch=10. If kv-cache off the failures drop to ~0.5%. Likely tokenization boundary + PTQ rounding causing different punctuation tokens at end-of-object.

Omar K: Short-term: implement a non-blocking repair step in the serving adapter that finds last balanced brace and strips trailing text before parsing. Long-term: run PTQ config sweep (per-tensor vs per-channel, clip ranges) and a tokenizer/bpe drift check.

Ivy (Canary): I've uploaded top-150 failing prompts to the eval harness (erun-57900X). Plan: run matrix fp16, ptq-int8(per-tensor), ptq-int8(per-channel), and ptq-int8 with kv-cache off. Also add a streaming-slice test (frame size 32 tokens).

ci-bot: Canary report: model=Sylph-v0.9-ptq(int8), samples=800, parse_fail=3.3%, mean_rt=145ms

Sam: We should not relax schema checks in canary. Proposal: keep strict linter, add rescue that is opt-in per-canary and tags rescued samples in telemetry. That preserves signal while reducing downstream breakage.

Tara L: Agreed. Action items: @Omar -> PTQ sweep + canary without kv-cache by EOD. @Ivy -> run eval matrix and attach failure histogram. @Sam -> prototype json_rescue adapter and ensure telemetry tag. Hold rollout until parse_fail <0.5% or rescue+telemetry accepted. Thanks.
